episode_title: How Do We Close the Flooring Skills Gap? with Shaun Wadsworth

real_qa.q: What is the Contract Flooring Association and how does it differ from CFJ?
real_qa.r: The Contract Flooring Association is a trade body representing the commercial flooring sector with membership categories in contracting, manufacturing, distribution, consultation, and training. It is not a publication like CFJ. The CFA provides support to members on guidance, training, retention, site conditions, winning work, marketing, insurances, and templates. The CFA logo serves as a sign of quality by association in a largely unregulated industry, and operates as soft regulation primarily built for contractors.
real_qa.requete: Contract Flooring Association CFA what is

real_qa.q: How many flooring fitters does the UK construction sector need over the next five years?
real_qa.r: Construction as a whole needs over 200,000 fitters over the next five years, of which approximately 40,000 to 41,000 are needed specifically for flooring. This figure covers people leaving the trade and retiring, as well as work coming in. The CFA estimates its membership represents about 12,500 fitters, but the sector cannot rely solely on apprentices to fill this gap.

real_qa.q: What are the main barriers preventing flooring fitters from attending training courses?
real_qa.r: The primary barrier is cost, which extends beyond just the course price to include loss of time, travel, and accommodation for those traveling from far away. For a £300 day course, the total expense can escalate into small holiday territory. Independent installers face additional pressure because they lose income on the day they attend training, whereas larger contractors can build training into budgets and matrices. Free training often fails because fitters prioritize paying jobs that come up on the day.
real_qa.requete: why flooring fitters don't attend training cost

real_qa.q: How many floor laying apprenticeship training providers operate across the UK?
real_qa.r: There are approximately nine floor laying apprenticeship training providers in the UK: two in Doncaster, one in Birmingham, one in Loughborough (FITTA), one in Newcastle, one in the South, one in Wales, and one in Scotland. FITTA only began delivering apprenticeships five years ago and has since added the East Midlands through a partnership with Web's Training.
real_qa.requete: floor laying apprenticeship training providers UK locations

real_qa.q: What percentage skills gap exists in the UK flooring sector for new fitters?
real_qa.r: Alan McEwan from FBall referenced a 17% skills gap relating to new fitters entering the industry. The CFA tracks employed and subcontracted fitters among its members and amplifies that data across the sector to measure the gap, which encompasses not just skills and labor shortages but also quarters, work planned, retention, payment timelines, and pre-qualification requirements.

guest.bio_context: Shaun Wadsworth has held the Deputy CEO role at the Contract Flooring Association since April, and continues to work extensively as Training Manager, overseeing all training delivery through the CFA and FITTA. He manages apprenticeship delivery, private courses, sponsor days, and member-based events from the training center in Loughborough, and is responsible for signposting training opportunities across the commercial flooring sector.
